seen.body:
## Behaviour
`qew pr ready NUMBER [--target T]` marks the caller's recorded draft PR ready, then re-reads the PR and verifies it is no longer a draft (still a draft afterwards is an indeterminate failure, exit 4, never success). A merged or closed PR is exit 2 and writes nothing. An already-ready PR is reported unchanged and writes nothing. A non-positive number is exit 2 before any ledger or forge call. A PR whose covered items include a draft is refused (exit 2). The command stays discoverable as a subcommand of `qew pr`.

## Scenarios
- golden: draft PR becomes ready, read back not draft, output `pr #N ready`. Prevents: reporting ready when the forge did not change.
- already ready: output says unchanged, forge mark call count zero. Prevents: redundant writes.
- merged and closed PRs: exit 2, zero writes. Prevents: touching finished PRs.
- stays draft after the write: exit 4 'still a draft'. Prevents: false success.
- non-positive number (0, -3): exit 2 before any call. Prevents: odd forge URLs.
- unrecorded number: exit 2 'not recorded' (exists for merge; assert for ready too).
- draft covered item: refused exit 2 naming `qew draft approve`. Prevents: readying a plan PR early.

## Reference coverage
Reference pr ready walk file: marks ready and verifies, human output, already ready, merged/closed refused, another login refused, teammate holds claims, teammate missing claim names take-over, stays draft indeterminate, non-positive number, creating a PR still works without the subcommand. 10 test functions (3 ownership ones go to pr-owner-rule; the last is a parser-compat check and is dropped).

## Qew today
Reduced: `mark_ready` refuses a draft item and relays forge errors, but there is no read-back, no already-ready no-op, no merged/closed refusal, no number validation, no test for `ready` at all (tests/test_pr_walk.py calls it only as setup).
seen.title: Complete `qew pr ready`: verify, idempotence, refusals, input checks
